Base directory for this skill: /Users/cyyeh/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/4.3.0/skills/brainstorming

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

## Overview

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
3. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
4. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
5. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
6. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];

    "Explore project context" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill";
}
```

**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**
- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**
- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why

**Presenting the design:**
- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

## After the Design

**Documentation:**
- Write the validated design to `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Implementation:**
- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Key Principles

- **One question at a time** - Don't overwhelm with multiple questions
- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible
- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs
- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

1→# DuckDB Data Agent
     2→
     3→> **Note:** This project is built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code)(using Opus 4.6 and [superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)) by more than 95% and human-reviewed by author.
     4→
     5→[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy)
     6→
     7→An AI-powered data analysis agent with a built-in SQL playground. Upload data files (CSV, JSON, Parquet, Excel) and ask questions in plain English, or switch to the SQL editor for direct queries — powered by [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) on a lightweight [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) backend with a React frontend. The app opens in Agent Mode by default so you can start analyzing data immediately.
     8→
     9→Each browser tab gets its own isolated, in-memory DuckDB session — uploaded data and query state are fully isolated between users and tabs, with idle sessions automatically cleaned up after 5 minutes of inactivity.
    10→
    11→## Features
    12→
    13→### General
    14→
    15→- **Per-user DuckDB sessions** — Each browser tab gets its own isolated in-memory DuckDB instance, identified by a `X-Session-ID` header generated client-side; data and state are never shared between users or tabs; idle sessions are automatically cleaned up after 5 minutes
    16→- **DuckDB SQL engine** — Fast, in-process analytical database on the backend
    17→- **Multi-format file upload** — Drag-and-drop or click to import CSV, JSON, Parquet, and Excel (.xlsx) files (default limit: 500 MB, configurable via `MAX_TOTAL_SIZE_BYTES` env var) with automatic schema detection; Excel workbooks with multiple sheets create one table per sheet; duplicate filename detection prevents accidental overwrites; the upload UI appears when no tables are loaded, and files can also be added via the sidebar upload button
    18→- **Sample dataset** — One-click load of the Titanic dataset to get started quickly
    19→- **Table sidebar** — Collapsible panel to browse tables, inspect columns, and view types
    20→- **Dark / light mode** — Toggle between dark and light themes with the sun/moon button in the header; respects your OS preference on first visit and remembers your choice across sessions
    21→- **Internationalization (i18n)** — Switch between English and Traditional Chinese with the EN/中 toggle in the header; auto-detects your OS language on first visit and remembers your choice across sessions
    22→
    23→### Agent Mode (default mode)
    24→
    25→- **Natural language queries** — Ask questions about your data in plain English; the agent writes and executes SQL for you
    26→- **Streaming responses** — Real-time token streaming powered by Claude via the [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
    27→- **Visible reasoning** — Collapsible thinking block shows the agent's intermediate steps and SQL queries
    28→- **Inline results** — Query results rendered inline within the conversation
    29→- **Edit & delete messages** — Hover over any user message to edit or delete it; editing re-sends the modified query with prior conversation as context, deleting rewinds the conversation to that point
    30→- **Credential proxy** — The backend runs a built-in Anthropic API reverse proxy; each agent session receives a short-lived UUID token instead of the real API key, so the Claude Code subprocess never has access to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; tokens are revoked immediately when the session ends (see [Security](#security))
    31→- **Privacy-conscious** — Requires an Anthropic API key stored in a server-side `.env` file; your data and credentials are never sent anywhere besides the Anthropic API
    32→- **Langfuse observability** (optional) — Built-in [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) tracing for monitoring agent interactions, with a one-click dashboard link in the UI
    33→
    34→### Editor Mode
    35→
    36→- **SQL query editor** — Write and execute queries with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
    37→- **Interactive results** — Sortable columns, per-column filters, and global search across results
    38→- **EXPLAIN support** — Markdown-rendered output for `EXPLAIN` and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` queries
    39→
    40→## Getting Started
    41→
    42→### Prerequisites
    43→
    44→- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20+
    45→- [Python](https://www.python.org/) 3.12+
    46→- [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/)
    47→
    48→### Installation
    49→
    50→```bash
    51→make install
    52→```
    53→
    54→Or install frontend and backend separately:
    55→
    56→```bash
    57→cd frontend && npm install
    58→cd backend && poetry install
    59→```
    60→
    61→### Configuration
    62→
    63→Copy the example environment file and add your credentials:
    64→
    65→```bash
    66→cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
    67→```
    68→
    69→Edit `backend/.env` and set your Anthropic API key:
    70→
    71→```
    72→ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
    73→ANTHROPIC_MODEL=sonnet              # optional, defaults to sonnet
    74→MAX_TOTAL_SIZE_BYTES=524288000      # optional, max upload size in bytes (default: 500 MB)
    75→```
    76→
    77→> `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` are only needed for the AI agent. The SQL playground works without them, but both require the backend running.
    78→
    79→#### Langfuse (optional)
    80→
    81→To enable agent tracing with [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/), add these to `backend/.env`:
    82→
    83→```
    84→LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-...
    85→LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-...
    86→LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com   # optional, defaults to cloud
    87→```
    88→
    89→When configured, every agent conversation is traced (LLM turns, tool calls, SQL execution) and a **Langfuse Traces** button appears in the agent panel header linking to your dashboard. When not configured, tracing is disabled with zero overhead.
    90→
    91→### Development
    92→
    93→Start both the frontend and backend:
    94→
    95→```bash
    96→make dev
    97→```
    98→
    99→Or run them separately:
   100→
   101→```bash
   102→make frontend   # http://localhost:5173
   103→make backend    # http://localhost:8000
   104→```
   105→
   106→Open http://localhost:5173 to use the app. The Vite dev server proxies `/api` requests to the backend automatically.
   107→
   108→## Production Build and Deployment
   109→
   110→The project ships as a single Docker image that bundles the React frontend and FastAPI backend. A multi-stage `Dockerfile` builds the frontend, then copies the output into the backend's static directory.
   111→
   112→### Build and run locally
   113→
   114→```bash
   115→docker build -t duckdb-data-agent .
   116→
   117→docker run -p 10000:10000 \
   118→  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... \
   119→  duckdb-data-agent
   120→```
   121→
   122→Add `-e LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... -e LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-...` to either command to enable Langfuse tracing.
   123→
   124→Open http://localhost:10000 to use the app.
   125→
   126→### Deploy to Render
   127→
   128→A `render.yaml` is included for one-click deployment on [Render](https://render.com/):
   129→
   130→1. Push this repo to GitHub.
   131→2. In Render, create a new **Blueprint** and connect the repo.
   132→3. Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the Render dashboard. Optionally set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to override the default model (`sonnet`). To enable Langfuse tracing, also set `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` and `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`.
   133→
   134→Render will build the Docker image and deploy it automatically on every push to `main`.
   135→
   136→## Security
   137→
   138→### Credential Proxy
   139→
   140→When the agent runs, the backend spawns a Claude Code subprocess via the Anthropic Agent SDK. A naive approach would pass `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` directly into that subprocess's environment — but any tool or shell command the agent executes could then read and exfiltrate the key.
   141→
   142→Instead, the backend runs a built-in reverse proxy at `/anthropic` that sits between Claude Code and `api.anthropic.com`:
   143→
   144→```
   145→Claude Code subprocess
   146→  → ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/anthropic
   147→  → ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<short-lived UUID token>
   148→        ↓
   149→FastAPI proxy (/anthropic/{path})
   150→  → validates UUID token
   151→  → swaps it for the real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
   152→  → forwards request to api.anthropic.com
   153→```
   154→
   155→**How it works:**
   156→
   157→1. Before each agent session, the backend mints a random UUID token with a 10-minute TTL.
   158→2. The token is injected into the subprocess environment as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; the real key is never exposed.
   159→3. The proxy validates every inbound request against the token store and substitutes the real key before forwarding upstream.
   160→4. When the session ends, the token is explicitly revoked in a `finally` block, regardless of success or error.
   161→5. A background task runs every 60 seconds to sweep any tokens that outlived their TTL.
   162→
   163→The subprocess only ever holds a single-session UUID. Even if a tool call reads the environment, all it gets is a temporary token scoped to that conversation.
   164→
   165→## Project Structure
   166→
   167→```
   168→├── frontend/               # React frontend
   169→│   ├── src/
   170→│   │   ├── components/     #   UI components (editor, results, sidebar, chat)
   171→│   │   ├── contexts/       #   React context providers (theme, language, agent, config, session)
   172→│   │   ├── hooks/          #   Custom hooks (useTheme, useTranslation, useAgent, useConfig)
   173→│   │   ├── agent/          #   Agent service (SSE event handling, session ID injection)
   174→│   │   ├── i18n/           #   Translation files (en.json, zh-TW.json)
   175→│   │   └── types.ts        #   Shared TypeScript interfaces
   176→│   ├── index.html          #   HTML entry point
   177→│   ├── package.json        #   npm config
   178→│   └── vite.config.ts      #   Vite bundler config
   179→├── backend/                # FastAPI backend
   180→│   └── app/
   181→│       ├── main.py         #   App setup, CORS, and background session cleanup loop
   182→│       ├── config.py       #   Environment variables (API key, model, upload limits)
   183→│       ├── database.py     #   DuckDB connection, query execution, and per-user SessionManager
   184→│       ├── agent.py        #   Agent loop & SSE streaming
   185→│       ├── proxy.py        #   Credential proxy: token store + /anthropic reverse proxy
   186→│       ├── tracing.py      #   Langfuse client wrapper & initialization
   187→│       ├── tools.py        #   Agent SDK tool definitions (execute_sql)
   188→│       ├── data/           #   Sample datasets (titanic.csv)
   189→│       └── routes/         #   API endpoints (tables, query, chat, config, langfuse status, heartbeat)
   190→├── Dockerfile              # Multi-stage production build
   191→├── render.yaml             # Render deployment config
   192→└── Makefile                # Dev commands (install, dev, clean)
   193→```
   194→
   195→## Tech Stack
   196→
   197→**Frontend**
   198→- [React](https://react.dev/) 18 + [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
   199→- [Vite](https://vite.dev/)
   200→
   201→**Backend**
   202→- [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) + [Uvicorn](https://www.uvicorn.org/)
   203→- [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) (Python)
   204→- [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
   205→- [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) (optional, for observability)
   206→
   207→## License
   208→
   209→[MIT](LICENSE.txt)

1→import asyncio

     3→from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
     4→from pathlib import Path
     5→
     6→from fastapi import FastAPI

     8→from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

    10→
    11→from app.routes import tables, query, chat, langfuse_status, config, session
    12→from app import proxy as proxy_module
    13→
    14→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    15→
    16→from app.session_manager import session_manager
    17→
    18→
    19→async def _cleanup_loop():
    20→    while True:
    21→        await asyncio.sleep(60)
    22→        removed = session_manager.cleanup_stale(ttl_seconds=300)
    23→        if removed:
    24→            logger.info("Background cleanup: removed %d stale sessions", removed)
    25→        proxy_removed = proxy_module.proxy_token_store.cleanup_expired()
    26→        if proxy_removed:
    27→            logger.info("Background cleanup: removed %d expired proxy tokens", proxy_removed)
    28→
    29→
    30→@asynccontextmanager
    31→async def lifespan(app):
    32→    task = asyncio.create_task(_cleanup_loop())
    33→    yield
    34→    task.cancel()
    35→
    36→
    37→app = FastAPI(title="DuckDB Data Agent API", lifespan=lifespan)
    38→
    39→app.add_middleware(
    40→    CORSMiddleware,
    41→    allow_origins=["*"],
    42→    allow_credentials=True,
    43→    allow_methods=["*"],

    47→app.include_router(tables.router)

1→import json
     2→import logging
     3→from typing import AsyncIterator
     4→
     5→from claude_agent_sdk import (
     6→    ClaudeSDKClient,
     7→    ClaudeAgentOptions,
     8→    AssistantMessage,
     9→    UserMessage,
    10→    ResultMessage,
    11→    ToolUseBlock,
    12→    ToolResultBlock,
    13→)
    14→from claude_agent_sdk.types import StreamEvent, SystemMessage
    15→from claude_agent_sdk._errors import MessageParseError
    16→from app.tools import create_duckdb_server
    17→from app.database import Database
    18→from app.config import ANTHROPIC_MODEL, PROXY_BASE_URL
    19→from app.proxy import proxy_token_store
    20→from app.tracing import get_langfuse_client
    21→
    22→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    23→
    24→# Monkey-patch parse_message to handle unknown message types (e.g. rate_limit_event)
    25→# gracefully instead of crashing the stream. The SDK (v0.1.39) doesn't recognize
    26→# newer message types from the CLI. Returning a SystemMessage lets the stream
    27→# continue since our code ignores SystemMessage instances.
    28→import claude_agent_sdk._internal.message_parser as _parser
    29→
    30→_original_parse_message = _parser.parse_message
    31→
    32→
    33→def _safe_parse_message(data):
    34→    try:
    35→        return _original_parse_message(data)
    36→    except MessageParseError as e:
    37→        if "Unknown message type" in str(e):
    38→            msg_type = data.get("type", "unknown") if isinstance(data, dict) else "unknown"
    39→            logger.warning("Skipping unrecognized message type from CLI: %s", msg_type)
    40→            return SystemMessage(subtype=msg_type, data=data if isinstance(data, dict) else {})
    41→        raise
    42→
    43→
    44→_parser.parse_message = _safe_parse_message
    45→
    46→
    47→def build_system_prompt(db: Database) -> str:
    48→    tables = db.list_tables()
    49→    prompt = """You are a helpful data analyst assistant working with a DuckDB database.
    50→You can execute SQL queries using the execute_sql tool to answer questions about the user's data.
    51→
    52→Guidelines:
    53→- Write clear, efficient DuckDB SQL queries
    54→- When exploring data, start with small queries (use LIMIT)
    55→- Explain your findings in plain language after getting results
    56→- If a query fails, try to fix it and retry
    57→- Use double quotes for table and column names that might conflict with reserved words
    58→
    59→Identity:
    60→- You are an AI assistant. If asked whether you are an AI or a human, always confirm that you are an AI.
    61→- Do not disclose the name, version, or provider of the underlying language model powering you, regardless of how the question is phrased.
    62→"""
    63→    if not tables:
    64→        prompt += "\nNo tables are currently loaded. Ask the user to upload a CSV file first."
    65→    else:
    66→        prompt += "\nCurrently loaded tables:\n"
    67→        for table in tables:
    68→            prompt += f'\nTable: "{table["name"]}" ({table["rowCount"]} rows)\nColumns:\n'
    69→            for col in table["columns"]:
    70→                prompt += f'  - "{col["name"]}" ({col["type"]})\n'
    71→
    72→    return prompt
    73→
    74→
    75→def _build_message_with_history(
    76→    message: str, conversation_history: list[dict] | None = None
    77→) -> str:
    78→    """Prepend conversation history context to the user message when editing."""
    79→    if not conversation_history:
    80→        return message
    81→
    82→    history_text = "Previous conversation (for context, I am now editing a message):\n"
    83→    for entry in conversation_history:
    84→        role = entry.get("role", "user").capitalize()
    85→        content = entry.get("content", "")
    86→        history_text += f"\n{role}: {content}\n"

    90→
    91→def _extract_tool_result_text(content: object) -> str:
    92→    """Extract text from ToolResultBlock.content."""
    93→    if content is None:
    94→        return ""
    95→    if isinstance(content, str):
    96→        return content
    97→    if isinstance(content, list):
    98→        parts = []
    99→        for item in content:
   100→            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("type") == "text":
   101→                parts.append(item.get("text", ""))
   102→        return "\n".join(parts)

   106→async def stream_chat(
   107→    message: str,
   108→    session_id: str | None = None,
   109→    db: Database | None = None,
   110→    conversation_history: list[dict] | None = None,
   111→    langfuse_session_id: str | None = None,
   112→) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
   113→    """Stream agent chat responses as SSE events."""
   114→    if db is None:
   115→        raise ValueError("db must be provided")
   116→    duckdb_server = create_duckdb_server(db)
   117→
   118→    logger.info("Using model: %s", ANTHROPIC_MODEL)
   119→
   120→    # Collect stderr from the CLI subprocess for debugging
   121→    stderr_lines: list[str] = []
   122→
   123→    # Use the --resume flag to continue an existing session
   124→    session_token = proxy_token_store.create_token()
   125→    options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
   126→        model=ANTHROPIC_MODEL,
   127→        system_prompt=build_system_prompt(db),
   128→        mcp_servers={"duckdb": duckdb_server},
   129→        allowed_tools=["mcp__duckdb__execute_sql"],
   130→        permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
   131→        max_turns=20,
   132→        include_partial_messages=True,
   133→        stderr=lambda line: stderr_lines.append(line),
   134→        env={
   135→            "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": session_token,
   136→            "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": f"{PROXY_BASE_URL}/anthropic",
   137→            # Scrub Langfuse credentials so the agent subprocess cannot
   138→            # read them from the inherited environment.
   139→            "LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY": "",
   140→            "LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY": "",
   141→        },
   142→        **({"resume": session_id} if session_id else {}),
   143→    )
   144→
   145→    # When editing, prepend conversation history to the user message
   146→    # instead of bloating the system prompt
   147→    query_message = _build_message_with_history(message, conversation_history)
   148→
   149→    client = ClaudeSDKClient(options=options)
   150→    # Will be set from the CLI's ResultMessage; use the passed-in value until then
   151→    actual_session_id = session_id
   152→
   153→    # --- Langfuse OTel tracing setup (conditional) ---
   154→    # Deferred: session_id is set after the CLI returns it in ResultMessage
   155→    langfuse = get_langfuse_client()
   156→    observation_ctx = None
   157→    propagate_ctx = None
   158→    if langfuse:
   159→        try:
   160→            trace_input: dict = {"message": message[:500]}
   161→            if conversation_history:
   162→                trace_input["conversation_history"] = conversation_history
   163→            observation_ctx = langfuse.start_as_current_observation(
   164→                name="agent-chat",
   165→                input=trace_input,
   166→                metadata={"model": ANTHROPIC_MODEL},
   167→            )
   168→            observation_ctx.__enter__()
   169→
   170→            # Propagate the stable conversation session_id for child spans
   171→            effective_langfuse_session_id = langfuse_session_id or session_id
   172→            if effective_langfuse_session_id:
   173→                from langfuse import propagate_attributes
   174→                propagate_ctx = propagate_attributes(session_id=effective_langfuse_session_id)
   175→                propagate_ctx.__enter__()
   176→        except Exception as e:
   177→            logger.debug("Failed to set up Langfuse tracing context: %s", e)
   178→            observation_ctx = None
   179→
   180→    try:
   181→        await client.connect()
   182→        await client.query(query_message, session_id=session_id or "default")
   183→
   184→        has_tool_calls = False
   185→        has_thinking = False
   186→        sql_result_ids: set[str] = set()
   187→        tool_names: dict[str, str] = {}
   188→
   189→        async for msg in client.receive_response():
   190→            if isinstance(msg, StreamEvent):
   191→                event = msg.event
   192→                event_type = event.get("type", "")
   193→
   194→                if event_type == "content_block_delta":
   195→                    delta = event.get("delta", {})
   196→                    delta_type = delta.get("type", "")
   197→                    if delta_type == "thinking_delta":
   198→                        text = delta.get("thinking", "")
   199→                        if text:
   200→                            yield f"event: thinking\ndata: {json.dumps({'text': text})}\n\n"
   201→                    elif delta_type == "text_delta":
   202→                        text = delta.get("text", "")
   203→                        event_name = "thinking" if not has_tool_calls else "answer"
   204→                        yield f"event: {event_name}\ndata: {json.dumps({'text': text})}\n\n"
   205→
   206→                elif event_type == "content_block_start":
   207→                    block = event.get("content_block", {})
   208→                    block_type = block.get("type")
   209→                    if block_type == "thinking":
   210→                        has_thinking = True
   211→                    elif block_type == "text":
   212→                        if has_thinking:
   213→                            yield f"event: thinking_done\ndata: {json.dumps({})}\n\n"
   214→                    elif block_type == "tool_use":
   215→                        has_thinking = False
   216→                        has_tool_calls = True
   217→
   218→            elif isinstance(msg, AssistantMessage):
   219→                for block in msg.content:
   220→                    if isinstance(block, ToolUseBlock):
   221→                        has_tool_calls = True
   222→                        tool_name = getattr(block, "name", "") or ""
   223→                        tool_names[block.id] = tool_name
   224→                        sql = block.input.get("sql", "")
   225→                        command = block.input.get("command", "")
   226→
   227→                        # Emit tool_call for ALL tool types
   228→                        tool_call_data: dict = {"id": block.id, "name": tool_name}
   229→                        if sql:
   230→                            tool_call_data["sql"] = sql
   231→                        if command:
   232→                            tool_call_data["command"] = command
   233→                        if not sql and not command:
   234→                            tool_call_data["input"] = block.input
   235→                        yield f"event: tool_call\ndata: {json.dumps(tool_call_data, default=str)}\n\n"
   236→
   237→                        # For SQL tools, execute query for structured results
   238→                        if sql:
   239→                            sql_result_ids.add(block.id)
   240→                            try:
   241→                                result = db.execute_query(sql)
   242→                                truncated = result["rows"][:100]
   243→                                yield f"event: tool_result\ndata: {json.dumps({'id': block.id, 'name': tool_name, 'sql': sql, 'columns': result['columns'], 'rows': truncated, 'rowCount': result['rowCount']}, default=str)}\n\n"
   244→                            except Exception as e:
   245→                                yield f"event: tool_result\ndata: {json.dumps({'id': block.id, 'name': tool_name, 'sql': sql, 'error': str(e)})}\n\n"
   246→
   247→            elif isinstance(msg, UserMessage):
   248→                # Capture tool results from the SDK for non-SQL tools
   249→                content = msg.content
   250→                if isinstance(content, list):
   251→                    for block in content:
   252→                        if isinstance(block, ToolResultBlock):
   253→                            if block.tool_use_id in sql_result_ids:
   254→                                continue
   255→                            output = _extract_tool_result_text(block.content)
   256→                            name = tool_names.get(block.tool_use_id, "")
   257→                            result_data: dict = {
   258→                                "id": block.tool_use_id,
   259→                                "name": name,
   260→                                "output": output,
   261→                            }
   262→                            if block.is_error:
   263→                                result_data["error"] = output
   264→                            yield f"event: tool_result\ndata: {json.dumps(result_data, default=str)}\n\n"
   265→
   266→            elif isinstance(msg, ResultMessage):
   267→                # Use the CLI's session_id so --resume can find it
   268→                actual_session_id = msg.session_id or actual_session_id
   269→                if msg.is_error and msg.result:
   270→                    yield f"event: error\ndata: {json.dumps({'message': msg.result})}\n\n"
   271→                yield f"event: done\ndata: {json.dumps({'session_id': actual_session_id})}\n\n"
   272→
   273→    except Exception as e:
   274→        error_msg = str(e)
   275→        if stderr_lines:
   276→            error_msg += f" | CLI stderr: {' '.join(stderr_lines[-5:])}"
   277→        logger.error("Agent error: %s", error_msg)
   278→        yield f"event: error\ndata: {json.dumps({'message': error_msg})}\n\n"
   279→    finally:
   280→        proxy_token_store.revoke_token(session_token)
   281→        # Update trace with the CLI's session_id so Langfuse session matches
   282→        if langfuse and observation_ctx:
   283→            try:
   284→                trace_session_id = langfuse_session_id or actual_session_id
   285→                langfuse.update_current_trace(
   286→                    session_id=trace_session_id,
   287→                    output={"session_id": actual_session_id},
   288→                )
   289→                if propagate_ctx:
   290→                    propagate_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
   291→                observation_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
   292→            except Exception as e:
   293→                logger.debug("Failed to finalize Langfuse trace: %s", e)
   294→            try:
   295→                langfuse.flush()
   296→            except Exception as e:
   297→                logger.debug("Failed to flush Langfuse: %s", e)
   298→
   299→        try:
   300→            await client.disconnect()
   301→        except Exception:
   302→            pass
   303→

1→import logging
     2→import uuid
     3→from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
     4→
     5→from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Request
     6→from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
     7→import httpx
     8→
     9→from app.config import ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
    10→
    11→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    12→
    13→ANTHROPIC_UPSTREAM = "https://api.anthropic.com"
    14→
    15→_SKIP_REQUEST_HEADERS = {
    16→    "host", "content-length", "transfer-encoding", "connection",
    17→    "x-api-key",         # client must not override billing identity
    18→    "anthropic-version", # proxy controls API version
    19→    # anthropic-beta is intentionally NOT blocked: Claude Code sends beta body
    20→    # fields (e.g. context_management) alongside the matching beta header, and
    21→    # Anthropic rejects those fields as "extra inputs" if the header is absent.
    22→}
    23→_SKIP_RESPONSE_HEADERS = {"transfer-encoding", "content-encoding", "connection"}
    24→
    25→
    26→class ProxyTokenStore:
    27→    def __init__(self, ttl_seconds: int = 600):
    28→        self._ttl = ttl_seconds
    29→        self._tokens: dict[str, datetime] = {}
    30→
    31→    def create_token(self) -> str:
    32→        token = str(uuid.uuid4())
    33→        self._tokens[token] = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(seconds=self._ttl)
    34→        return token
    35→
    36→    def validate_token(self, token: str) -> bool:
    37→        # Tokens are intentionally multi-use: Claude Code makes many API calls
    38→        # per session, all protected by the same UUID. The token is valid for
    39→        # the session TTL (600s safety net) but is explicitly revoked by
    40→        # proxy_token_store.revoke_token() in agent.py's finally block when
    41→        # the Claude Code subprocess exits. Do not make single-use.
    42→        expiry = self._tokens.get(token)
    43→        if expiry is None:
    44→            return False
    45→        if datetime.now(timezone.utc) > expiry:
    46→            self._tokens.pop(token, None)
    47→            return False
    48→        return True
    49→
    50→    def revoke_token(self, token: str) -> None:
    51→        self._tokens.pop(token, None)
    52→
    53→    def cleanup_expired(self) -> int:
    54→        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    55→        expired = [t for t, exp in self._tokens.items() if now > exp]
    56→        for t in expired:
    57→            del self._tokens[t]
    58→        return len(expired)
    59→
    60→
    61→proxy_token_store = ProxyTokenStore()
    62→
    63→router = APIRouter(prefix="/anthropic")
    64→
    65→
    66→@router.api_route("/{path:path}", methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "PATCH"])
    67→async def proxy_anthropic(path: str, request: Request):
    68→    # Claude Code CLI sends the API key as x-api-key (Anthropic SDK default).
    69→    # Fall back to Authorization: Bearer for other clients.
    70→    session_token = (
    71→        request.headers.get("x-api-key")
    72→        or request.headers.get("authorization", "")[len("Bearer "):]
    73→        or None
    74→    )
    75→    if not session_token or not proxy_token_store.validate_token(session_token):
    76→        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid or expired session token")
    77→
    78→    headers = {
    79→        k: v for k, v in request.headers.items()
    80→        if k.lower() not in _SKIP_REQUEST_HEADERS
    81→    }
    82→    headers["x-api-key"] = ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
    83→    headers["anthropic-version"] = "2023-06-01"
    84→
    85→    body = await request.body()
    86→
    87→    # Use a fresh client per request: streaming responses that are cut short
    88→    # (e.g. client disconnects) leave connections in a partial read state, and
    89→    # reusing a shared SSL context across those connections causes
    90→    # SSLV3_ALERT_BAD_RECORD_MAC / record layer failure errors.
    91→    # Query params are intentionally NOT forwarded — Claude Code appends
    92→    # internal params (e.g. ?beta=true) that Anthropic rejects as "extra inputs".
    93→    client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(300.0))
    94→    try:
    95→        upstream_req = client.build_request(
    96→            method=request.method,
    97→            url=f"{ANTHROPIC_UPSTREAM}/{path}",
    98→            headers=headers,
    99→            content=body,
   100→        )
   101→        upstream_resp = await client.send(upstream_req, stream=True)
   102→
   103→        response_headers = {
   104→            k: v for k, v in upstream_resp.headers.items()
   105→            if k.lower() not in _SKIP_RESPONSE_HEADERS
   106→        }
   107→
   108→        async def body_generator():
   109→            try:
   110→                async for chunk in upstream_resp.aiter_bytes():
   111→                    yield chunk
   112→            finally:
   113→                await upstream_resp.aclose()
   114→                await client.aclose()
   115→
   116→        return StreamingResponse(
   117→            body_generator(),
   118→            status_code=upstream_resp.status_code,
   119→            headers=response_headers,
   120→        )
   121→    except Exception:
   122→        await client.aclose()
   123→        logger.exception("Proxy request to upstream failed: %s %s", request.method, path)
   124→        raise
   125→

1→import json
     2→from typing import Any
     3→from claude_agent_sdk import tool, create_sdk_mcp_server
     4→from app.database import Database
     5→
     6→MAX_RESULT_ROWS = 100
     7→
     8→
     9→def create_duckdb_server(db: Database):
    10→    @tool(
    11→        "execute_sql",
    12→        "Execute a SQL query against the DuckDB database. Use this to query loaded tables, "
    13→        "create views, or run any valid DuckDB SQL. Results are returned as JSON with columns, "
    14→        "rows, and rowCount.",
    15→        {"sql": str},
    16→    )
    17→    async def execute_sql(args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    18→        sql = args["sql"]
    19→        try:
    20→            result = db.execute_query(sql)
    21→            truncated_rows = result["rows"][:MAX_RESULT_ROWS]
    22→            result_json = {
    23→                "status": "success",
    24→                "columns": result["columns"],
    25→                "rows": truncated_rows,
    26→                "rowCount": result["rowCount"],
    27→            }
    28→            content_text = json.dumps(result_json, default=str)
    29→            return {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": content_text}]}
    30→        except Exception as e:
    31→            error_json = {"status": "error", "error": str(e)}
    32→            return {
    33→                "content": [{"type": "text", "text": json.dumps(error_json)}],
    34→                "is_error": True,
    35→            }
    36→
    37→    return create_sdk_mcp_server(
    38→        name="duckdb",
    39→        version="1.0.0",
    40→        tools=[execute_sql],
    41→    )
    42→

1→import csv
     2→import duckdb
     3→import os
     4→import re
     5→import tempfile
     6→from typing import Any
     7→
     8→SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS = {".csv", ".json", ".parquet", ".xlsx"}
     9→
    10→
    11→class Database:
    12→    def __init__(self):
    13→        self.conn = duckdb.connect(":memory:")
    14→
    15→    def execute_query(self, sql: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    16→        """Execute a SQL query and return results as dict with columns, rows, rowCount."""
    17→        result = self.conn.execute(sql)
    18→        if result is None:
    19→            return {"columns": [], "rows": [], "rowCount": 0}
    20→        columns = [desc[0] for desc in result.description] if result.description else []
    21→        rows = [dict(zip(columns, row)) for row in result.fetchall()] if columns else []
    22→        return {"columns": columns, "rows": rows, "rowCount": len(rows)}
    23→
    24→    def load_csv(self, file_bytes: bytes, filename: str, table_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    25→        """Load a CSV file into a DuckDB table. Returns table info."""
    26→        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".csv", delete=False) as tmp:
    27→            tmp.write(file_bytes)
    28→            tmp_path = tmp.name
    29→        try:
    30→            self.conn.execute(
    31→                f'CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE "{table_name}" AS SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto(\'{tmp_path}\')'
    32→            )
    33→        finally:
    34→            os.unlink(tmp_path)
    35→        return self.get_table_info(table_name)
    36→
    37→    def load_json(self, file_bytes: bytes, filename: str, table_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    38→        """Load a JSON file (array of objects) into a DuckDB table. Returns table info."""
    39→        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".json", delete=False) as tmp:
    40→            tmp.write(file_bytes)
    41→            tmp_path = tmp.name
    42→        try:
    43→            self.conn.execute(
    44→                f'CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE "{table_name}" AS SELECT * FROM read_json_auto(\'{tmp_path}\')'
    45→            )
    46→        finally:
    47→            os.unlink(tmp_path)
    48→        return self.get_table_info(table_name)
    49→
    50→    def load_parquet(self, file_bytes: bytes, filename: str, table_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    51→        """Load a Parquet file into a DuckDB table. Returns table info."""
    52→        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".parquet", delete=False) as tmp:
    53→            tmp.write(file_bytes)
    54→            tmp_path = tmp.name
    55→        try:
    56→            self.conn.execute(
    57→                f'CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE "{table_name}" AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet(\'{tmp_path}\')'
    58→            )
    59→        finally:
    60→            os.unlink(tmp_path)
    61→        return self.get_table_info(table_name)
    62→
    63→    def load_excel(self, file_bytes: bytes, filename: str, base_table_name: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    64→        """Load an Excel file into DuckDB tables (one per sheet). Returns list of table infos."""
    65→        import openpyxl
    66→
    67→        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".xlsx", delete=False) as tmp:
    68→            tmp.write(file_bytes)
    69→            tmp_path = tmp.name
    70→        try:
    71→            wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(tmp_path, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    72→            sheet_names = wb.sheetnames
    73→            results = []
    74→            for sheet_name in sheet_names:
    75→                ws = wb[sheet_name]
    76→                rows = list(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True))
    77→                if not rows:
    78→                    continue
    79→                # Sanitize sheet name for table name
    80→                sanitized_sheet = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_]", "_", sheet_name.lower())
    81→                sanitized_sheet = re.sub(r"_+", "_", sanitized_sheet).strip("_")
    82→                table_name = f"{base_table_name}_{sanitized_sheet}" if len(sheet_names) > 1 else base_table_name
    83→                # Write sheet data to temp CSV
    84→                with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", suffix=".csv", delete=False, newline="") as csv_tmp:
    85→                    writer = csv.writer(csv_tmp)
    86→                    for row in rows:
    87→                        writer.writerow(row)
    88→                    csv_tmp_path = csv_tmp.name
    89→                try:
    90→                    self.conn.execute(
    91→                        f'CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE "{table_name}" AS SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto(\'{csv_tmp_path}\')'
    92→                    )
    93→                    results.append(self.get_table_info(table_name))
    94→                finally:
    95→                    os.unlink(csv_tmp_path)
    96→            wb.close()
    97→            if not results:
    98→                raise ValueError("Excel file contains no data")
    99→            return results
   100→        finally:
   101→            os.unlink(tmp_path)
   102→
   103→    def load_file(self, file_bytes: bytes, filename: str, table_name: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   104→        """Dispatch file loading based on extension. Returns list of table infos."""
   105→        ext = os.path.splitext(filename)[1].lower()
   106→        if ext == ".csv":
   107→            return [self.load_csv(file_bytes, filename, table_name)]
   108→        elif ext == ".json":
   109→            return [self.load_json(file_bytes, filename, table_name)]
   110→        elif ext == ".parquet":
   111→            return [self.load_parquet(file_bytes, filename, table_name)]
   112→        elif ext == ".xlsx":
   113→            return self.load_excel(file_bytes, filename, table_name)
   114→        else:
   115→            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported file format: {ext}")
   116→
   117→    def get_table_info(self, table_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
   118→        """Get info about a specific table."""
   119→        cols_result = self.conn.execute(f'DESCRIBE "{table_name}"')
   120→        columns = [
   121→            {"name": row[0], "type": row[1]}
   122→            for row in cols_result.fetchall()
   123→        ]
   124→        count_result = self.conn.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{table_name}"')
   125→        row_count = count_result.fetchone()[0]
   126→        return {"name": table_name, "columns": columns, "rowCount": row_count}
   127→
   128→    def list_tables(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   129→        """List all tables with their schema info."""
   130→        tables_result = self.conn.execute("SHOW TABLES")
   131→        table_names = [row[0] for row in tables_result.fetchall()]
   132→        return [self.get_table_info(name) for name in table_names]
   133→
   134→    def drop_table(self, table_name: str) -> None:
   135→        """Drop a table."""
   136→        self.conn.execute(f'DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "{table_name}"')
   137→
   138→    def load_sample_data(self, csv_path: str, table_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
   139→        """Load sample CSV from a file path."""
   140→        self.conn.execute(
   141→            f'CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE "{table_name}" AS SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto(\'{csv_path}\')'
   142→        )
   143→        return self.get_table_info(table_name)
   144→

1→import logging
     2→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     3→from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
     4→
     5→from app.database import Database
     6→
     7→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
     8→
     9→
    10→@dataclass
    11→class SessionEntry:
    12→    db: Database
    13→    last_seen_at: datetime = field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc))
    14→
    15→
    16→class SessionManager:
    17→    def __init__(self) -> None:
    18→        self._sessions: dict[str, SessionEntry] = {}
    19→
    20→    def get_or_create(self, session_id: str) -> Database:
    21→        if session_id not in self._sessions:
    22→            logger.info("Creating new session: %s", session_id)
    23→            self._sessions[session_id] = SessionEntry(db=Database())
    24→        else:
    25→            self._sessions[session_id].last_seen_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    26→        return self._sessions[session_id].db
    27→
    28→    def touch(self, session_id: str) -> bool:
    29→        if session_id not in self._sessions:
    30→            return False
    31→        self._sessions[session_id].last_seen_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    32→        return True
    33→
    34→    def destroy(self, session_id: str) -> None:
    35→        if session_id not in self._sessions:
    36→            return
    37→        try:
    38→            self._sessions[session_id].db.conn.close()
    39→        except Exception:
    40→            pass
    41→        del self._sessions[session_id]
    42→        logger.info("Destroyed session: %s", session_id)
    43→
    44→    def cleanup_stale(self, ttl_seconds: int = 300) -> int:
    45→        cutoff = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(seconds=ttl_seconds)
    46→        stale = [
    47→            sid for sid, entry in self._sessions.items()
    48→            if entry.last_seen_at < cutoff
    49→        ]
    50→        for sid in stale:
    51→            self.destroy(sid)
    52→        return len(stale)
    53→
    54→
    55→session_manager = SessionManager()
    56→

1→# Credential Proxy Design
     2→
     3→**Date:** 2026-02-21
     4→**Status:** Approved
     5→
     6→## Problem
     7→
     8→The server runs `claude-agent-sdk` which spawns Claude Code CLI as a subprocess. The subprocess inherits the parent process environment, including `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. A malicious user could craft a prompt to extract this token (e.g., `import os; print(os.environ)`), compromising the shared server account.
     9→
    10→## Solution
    11→
    12→A local reverse proxy runs inside the FastAPI app. Each chat session receives a short-lived UUID token. The Claude Code subprocess is given this UUID plus a `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointing to the local proxy. The proxy validates the UUID and swaps it for the real `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` before forwarding to `api.anthropic.com`.
    13→
    14→Even if a user extracts the UUID via prompt injection, it is useless outside `localhost` and expires when the chat session ends.
    15→
    16→## Architecture
    17→
    18→```
    19→[Server startup]
    20→  1. Read real token from CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN env var → store in memory
    21→
    22→[POST /api/chat]
    23→  2. Generate session UUID token
    24→  3. Register UUID → {expiry} in ActiveSessionTokens (TTL = chat session)
    25→  4. Pass to ClaudeAgentOptions(
    26→       env={
    27→         "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN": "<session-uuid>",
    28→         "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:10000/anthropic",
    29→       }
    30→     )
    31→  5. Claude Code subprocess sends Bearer <session-uuid> to local proxy
    32→
    33→[/anthropic/{path:path}]
    34→  6. Extract Bearer token from Authorization header
    35→  7. Validate it's a registered, non-expired session UUID
    36→  8. Replace Authorization → "Bearer <real CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN>"
    37→  9. Forward full request + body to https://api.anthropic.com/{path}
    38→ 10. Stream response back to Claude Code subprocess
    39→
    40→[SSE done/error event in agent.py]
    41→ 11. Revoke session UUID from ActiveSessionTokens
    42→```
    43→
    44→## Components
    45→
    46→| File | Change |
    47→|---|---|
    48→| `backend/app/proxy.py` | New — `ProxyTokenStore` + `/anthropic/{path}` FastAPI router |
    49→| `backend/app/agent.py` | Inject `env=` in `ClaudeAgentOptions`; accept token arg; revoke on done/error |
    50→| `backend/app/main.py` | Include proxy router |
    51→| `backend/app/config.py` | Read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from env |
    52→
    53→## Key Details
    54→
    55→### Env injection
    56→
    57→`subprocess_cli.py` builds the subprocess env as:
    58→```python
    59→process_env = {**os.environ, **options.env, ...}
    60→```
    61→`options.env` overrides win, so setting `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in `options.env` prevents the subprocess from seeing the real token in `os.environ`.
    62→
    63→### Token store
    64→
    65→In-memory dict: `{uuid: expiry_datetime}`. Tokens are created at chat start and deleted on `done`/`error` SSE events. No persistence needed — tokens are ephemeral.
    66→
    67→### Proxy forwarding
    68→
    69→Uses `httpx.AsyncClient` to forward the full request (method, headers, body) to `https://api.anthropic.com`, streaming the response back. The only header modification is replacing `Authorization`.
    70→
    71→### Security properties
    72→
    73→- Subprocess never sees real `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`
    74→- UUID token is useless outside `localhost`
    75→- Token expires at session end (revoked explicitly, not just by TTL)
    76→- No OAuth refresh logic needed — proxy forwards the long-lived token as-is
    77→
    78→## Out of Scope
    79→
    80→- Per-user OAuth (all users share one server account)
    81→- Rate limiting per session (separate concern)
    82→- Persistent token storage
    83→

     4→from app.config import LANGFUSE_ENABLED, LANGFUSE_BASE_URL

     7→

    10→
    11→def _init_langfuse():
    12→    """Initialize Langfuse with OTel auto-instrumentation for Claude Agent SDK."""
    13→    global _langfuse_client
    14→    if not LANGFUSE_ENABLED:
    15→        logger.info("Langfuse not configured, tracing disabled")
    16→        return
    17→
    18→    # Set OTel env vars so langsmith routes traces through Langfuse.
    19→    # Must be set before any langsmith import to avoid LRU cache issues.
    20→    for key, val in {
    21→        "LANGSMITH_OTEL_ENABLED": "true",
    22→        "LANGSMITH_OTEL_ONLY": "true",
    23→        "LANGSMITH_TRACING": "true",
    24→    }.items():
    25→        os.environ.setdefault(key, val)
    26→
    27→    try:
    28→        from langfuse import get_client
    29→
    30→        _langfuse_client = get_client()
    31→
    32→        # Scrub Langfuse credentials from os.environ so they cannot leak
    33→        # to agent subprocesses via environment inheritance.  The client
    34→        # object already holds the credentials internally.
    35→        for _key in ("LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY", "LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY"):
    36→            os.environ.pop(_key, None)
    37→
    38→        if _langfuse_client.auth_check():
    39→            logger.info("Langfuse connected successfully")
    40→        else:
    41→            logger.warning("Langfuse auth check failed, tracing disabled")
    42→            _langfuse_client = None
    43→            return
    44→
    45→        # Suppress harmless warnings from langsmith/OTel integration BEFORE

### 2. PROJECT PURPOSE & DESCRIPTION

**DuckDB Data Agent** is an AI-powered data analysis platform with two operational modes:

**Agent Mode (default):**
- Ask questions about data in plain English
- Claude Code (Opus 4.6) writes and executes SQL automatically
- Streaming responses with visible reasoning (collapsible thinking blocks)
- Real-time token streaming via Anthropic Agent SDK
- Edit/delete conversation messages with context preservation

**Editor Mode:**
- Direct SQL query editor with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter execution
- Interactive results: sortable columns, per-column filters, global search
- EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE support with markdown rendering

**Data Management:**
- Multi-format file upload: CSV, JSON, Parquet, Excel (.xlsx)
- Automatic schema detection
- Excel workbooks create one table per sheet
- Duplicate filename detection
- Configurable max upload size (default 500 MB)
- Sample Titanic dataset for quick-start

**UX Features:**
- Dark/light mode toggle (respects OS preference on first visit)
- Internationalization: English and Traditional Chinese
- Per-user isolated DuckDB sessions (in-memory, fully isolated)
- Idle session auto-cleanup after 5 minutes
- Langfuse observability integration (optional)

---

### 3. HOW CLAUDE CODE IS INVOKED

Claude Code is invoked via the **Anthropic Agent SDK** (Python client) in `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/backend/app/agent.py`:

**Key invocation code (lines 106-182 in agent.py):**
```python
# ClaudeSDKClient wraps the Claude Code subprocess
client = ClaudeSDKClient(options=ClaudeAgentOptions(
    model=ANTHROPIC_MODEL,
    system_prompt=build_system_prompt(db),
    mcp_servers={"duckdb": duckdb_server},           # DuckDB tool
    allowed_tools=["mcp__duckdb__execute_sql"],
    permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
    max_turns=20,
    include_partial_messages=True,
    stderr=lambda line: stderr_lines.append(line),
    env={
        "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": session_token,          # Short-lived UUID token
        "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": f"{PROXY_BASE_URL}/anthropic",  # Local proxy
        "LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY": "",                   # Scrubbed from env
        "LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY": "",
    },
    **({"resume": session_id} if session_id else {}),
))

await client.connect()
await client.query(query_message, session_id=session_id or "default")
```

**Process:**
1. Backend FastAPI route `/api/chat` receives user message
2. Creates short-lived UUID token via `proxy_token_store.create_token()`
3. Spawns Claude Code subprocess with UUID (not real API key)
4. Subprocess talks to `http://127.0.0.1:10000/anthropic` (local proxy)
5. Proxy validates UUID → swaps for real `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → forwards to api.anthropic.com
6. MCP server executes `execute_sql` tool (defined in `/backend/app/tools.py`)
7. SQL results returned inline within streaming response
8. Streams as SSE events: `thinking`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `answer`, `done`
9. On completion or error, token is explicitly revoked in `finally` block

**Tool Definition** (`/backend/app/tools.py`):
- Single MCP tool: `execute_sql` 
- Takes SQL string as input
- Returns columns, rows, row count as JSON
- Errors are caught and returned as `is_error: True`

- Base: `node:20-slim`
- Installs npm deps, builds React app with Vite
- Output: `/app/dist/` (static files)

**Stage 2: Backend with embedded frontend**

- Copies built frontend into `static/` directory
- Creates non-root `appuser` (Claude CLI refuses `--dangerously-skip-permissions` as root)
- Exposes port 10000
- CMD: `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 10000`

**Deployment:**
- Docker build locally or via CI/CD
- Render.com deployment configured in `render.yaml` (one-click deploy)
- Environment vars: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `LANGFUSE_*`, `MAX_TOTAL_SIZE_BYTES`

- Skill access: `claude-developer-platform`

---

### 8. TECH STACK SUMMARY

**Backend:**
- FastAPI 0.129.0 + Uvicorn (ASGI server)
- DuckDB 1.4.4 (in-process analytical SQL engine)
- claude-agent-sdk 0.1.38 (Claude Code subprocess wrapper)
- python-dotenv (env config)
- Langfuse 3.0.0 + langsmith (observability/OTel)
- openpyxl (Excel support)
- Python 3.12+

**Frontend:**
- React 18 + TypeScript
- Vite (fast bundler)
- CSS (inline styles in components)
- Internationalization (custom i18n with JSON files)

**Database:**
- DuckDB (in-memory, per-session)
- No persistence layer (data is ephemeral per tab)

**Deployment:**
- Docker (multi-stage)
- Render.com (optional)
- Cloudflare/Anthropic proxy integration for credential isolation

---

### 9. ARCHITECTURAL HIGHLIGHTS

**Credential Proxy (Security):**
- Each agent session gets a UUID token (10-minute TTL default)
- Claude Code subprocess receives UUID + local proxy URL
- Proxy validates UUID → swaps for real `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → forwards
- Token revoked immediately on session end
- Real credentials never exposed to subprocess

**Session Management:**
- Per-tab isolated DuckDB in-memory instances
- Session ID generated client-side (X-Session-ID header)
- Server-side SessionManager tracks connections
- 5-minute idle cleanup (configurable)
- No data sharing between users/tabs

**Streaming & Real-time:**
- Agent responses streamed as Server-Sent Events (SSE)
- Thinking blocks rendered collapsibly
- Tool calls/results shown inline
- Conversation history editable (re-sends with prior context)

**Observability:**
- Optional Langfuse tracing (OTel auto-instrumentation)
- Per-session trace IDs
- Visible dashboard link in UI when enabled

---

### 2. PROJECT PURPOSE & DESCRIPTION

**DuckDB Data Agent** is an AI-powered data analysis platform with two operational modes:

**Agent Mode (default):**
- Ask questions about data in plain English
- Claude Code (Opus 4.6) writes and executes SQL automatically
- Streaming responses with visible reasoning (collapsible thinking blocks)
- Real-time token streaming via Anthropic Agent SDK
- Edit/delete conversation messages with context preservation

**Editor Mode:**
- Direct SQL query editor with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter execution
- Interactive results: sortable columns, per-column filters, global search
- EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE support with markdown rendering

**Data Management:**
- Multi-format file upload: CSV, JSON, Parquet, Excel (.xlsx)
- Automatic schema detection
- Excel workbooks create one table per sheet
- Duplicate filename detection
- Configurable max upload size (default 500 MB)
- Sample Titanic dataset for quick-start

**UX Features:**
- Dark/light mode toggle (respects OS preference on first visit)
- Internationalization: English and Traditional Chinese
- Per-user isolated DuckDB sessions (in-memory, fully isolated)
- Idle session auto-cleanup after 5 minutes
- Langfuse observability integration (optional)

---

### 3. HOW CLAUDE CODE IS INVOKED

Claude Code is invoked via the **Anthropic Agent SDK** (Python client) in `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/backend/app/agent.py`:

**Key invocation code (lines 106-182 in agent.py):**
```python
# ClaudeSDKClient wraps the Claude Code subprocess
client = ClaudeSDKClient(options=ClaudeAgentOptions(
    model=ANTHROPIC_MODEL,
    system_prompt=build_system_prompt(db),
    mcp_servers={"duckdb": duckdb_server},           # DuckDB tool
    allowed_tools=["mcp__duckdb__execute_sql"],
    permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
    max_turns=20,
    include_partial_messages=True,
    stderr=lambda line: stderr_lines.append(line),
    env={
        "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": session_token,          # Short-lived UUID token
        "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": f"{PROXY_BASE_URL}/anthropic",  # Local proxy
        "LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY": "",                   # Scrubbed from env
        "LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY": "",
    },
    **({"resume": session_id} if session_id else {}),
))

await client.connect()
await client.query(query_message, session_id=session_id or "default")
```

**Process:**
1. Backend FastAPI route `/api/chat` receives user message
2. Creates short-lived UUID token via `proxy_token_store.create_token()`
3. Spawns Claude Code subprocess with UUID (not real API key)
4. Subprocess talks to `http://127.0.0.1:10000/anthropic` (local proxy)
5. Proxy validates UUID → swaps for real `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → forwards to api.anthropic.com
6. MCP server executes `execute_sql` tool (defined in `/backend/app/tools.py`)
7. SQL results returned inline within streaming response
8. Streams as SSE events: `thinking`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `answer`, `done`
9. On completion or error, token is explicitly revoked in `finally` block

**Tool Definition** (`/backend/app/tools.py`):
- Single MCP tool: `execute_sql` 
- Takes SQL string as input
- Returns columns, rows, row count as JSON
- Errors are caught and returned as `is_error: True`

Good, now I have a clear picture. Let me propose approaches.

---

## Proposed Approaches

Here are 3 architectural approaches for running Claude Code inside a gVisor-sandboxed container:

### Approach 1: Sidecar Container with Agent Wrapper (Recommended)

**Architecture:** Build a lightweight "agent sidecar" Docker image containing only Node.js + Claude CLI. On each session, the backend spawns a new container from this image with gVisor runtime. The container runs a thin HTTP server (Express/Fastify) that wraps the Claude Agent SDK, accepting queries and streaming responses back as SSE. The host backend orchestrates container lifecycle via Docker SDK for Python.

**Pros:**
- Clean separation: container has minimal surface area (Node.js + Claude CLI only)
- Reuses your existing SSE streaming model — frontend needs zero changes
- The thin HTTP wrapper is simple (~50-100 lines)
- Container talks to host proxy for API credentials and host MCP server for DuckDB — no secrets or data inside container
- gVisor intercepts all syscalls from Claude Code's bash/file tools

**Cons:**
- Requires building and maintaining a separate Docker image for the sidecar
- ~2-5s cold start per session for container creation
- Need to manage Docker networking (container → host proxy, container → host MCP)

---

### Approach 2: Docker-in-Docker with Existing Dockerfile

**Architecture:** Run the entire existing application stack inside a gVisor container, and spawn Claude Code subprocesses inside it the same way you do today (via Agent SDK). The outer container acts as the sandbox boundary.

**Pros:**
- Minimal code changes — the existing subprocess model stays the same
- No new images to build or HTTP wrappers to write

**Cons:**
- Coarser isolation — the entire backend runs inside the container, not just Claude Code
- Harder to do per-session containers (each session would need its own full backend instance)
- Heavier containers (Python + Node.js + FastAPI + DuckDB + Claude CLI)
- Doesn't truly separate Claude Code from the host backend

---

### Approach 3: Remote Claude Code via SSH/Exec

**Architecture:** Use `docker exec` to run Claude Code commands inside a pre-created gVisor container. The backend uses Docker SDK to create containers and exec commands into them, capturing stdout/stderr for streaming.

**Pros:**
- No HTTP wrapper needed inside the container
- Closest to current subprocess model
- Slightly simpler container image (no HTTP server needed)

**Cons:**
- `docker exec` streaming is harder to manage than HTTP SSE
- Error handling and lifecycle management is more complex
- Harder to cleanly separate concerns
- `docker exec` has its own security considerations

---

**My recommendation is Approach 1 (Sidecar Container with Agent Wrapper)** because it provides the cleanest isolation boundary — only Claude Code runs inside the sandbox, with no access to secrets, host filesystem, or DuckDB data. The HTTP interface is simple to build and aligns with your existing streaming architecture.

## Design Section 2: Sidecar Container Image

**Image contents (minimal):**
- Base: `node:20-slim`
- Claude CLI: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`
- Thin HTTP wrapper: `agent-server.js` (~80-100 lines)
- No Python, no DuckDB, no application code

**Dockerfile** (`sidecar/Dockerfile`):
```dockerfile
FROM node:20-slim
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
WORKDIR /app
COPY agent-server.js .
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "agent-server.js"]
```

**HTTP API (`agent-server.js`):**

| Endpoint | Method | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `/health` | GET | Readiness probe. Returns 200 when ready. |
| `/query` | POST | Accept `{message, session_id, system_prompt, mcp_servers, model}`. Stream response as SSE (same event types: `thinking`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `answer`, `done`). |
| `/stop` | POST | Gracefully stop the current query / session. |

**Environment variables passed at container creation (not baked in):**
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — the short-lived UUID token (from credential proxy)
- `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` — host proxy URL (e.g., `http://host.docker.internal:10000/anthropic`)
- `MCP_SERVER_URL` — host MCP endpoint for DuckDB tool

**What's NOT in the container:**
- No real API keys
- No uploaded data files
- No host filesystem mounts
- No Python runtime
- No DuckDB

## Design Section 3: Container Manager

New module `backend/app/container_manager.py` — manages the lifecycle of sidecar containers via the Docker SDK for Python (`docker` package).

**Class: `ContainerManager`**

```python
class ContainerManager:
    """Manages per-session gVisor-sandboxed sidecar containers."""

    def __init__(self, config: ContainerConfig):
        self.client = docker.from_env()
        self.config = config
        self.containers: dict[str, ContainerInfo] = {}  # session_id → container

    async def create(self, session_id: str, env: dict) -> ContainerInfo:
        """Spin up a new sidecar container for a session."""

    async def health_check(self, session_id: str) -> bool:
        """Check if the container's /health endpoint responds."""

    async def query(self, session_id: str, message: str, ...) -> AsyncIterator[SSEEvent]:
        """Send a query to the sidecar and stream SSE response back."""

    async def stop(self, session_id: str) -> None:
        """Stop and remove the container for a session."""

    async def cleanup_expired(self) -> None:
        """Remove containers that have exceeded max lifetime."""
```

**Container creation parameters:**
- Image: `duckdb-agent-sidecar:latest` (pre-built)
- Runtime: `runsc` (gVisor)
- Memory limit: configurable (default 256MB)
- CPU limit: configurable (default 0.5)
- Network: custom Docker bridge (restricted — only host proxy + host MCP accessible)
- No volume mounts
- No privileged mode
- Read-only root filesystem
- Auto-remove on stop
- Max lifetime: configurable (default 10 minutes)

**Integration with existing `agent.py`:**
- `stream_chat()` currently creates a `ClaudeSDKClient` directly
- Will be refactored to call `container_manager.create()` + `container_manager.query()` instead
- SSE events from sidecar are forwarded to the frontend unchanged
- Token creation/revocation via credential proxy stays the same

**New config variables** (in `config.py`):
```
CONTAINER_ENABLED=true              # Feature flag to enable/disable containerization
REDACTED:latest
CONTAINER_RUNTIME=runsc             # gVisor runtime
CONTAINER_MEMORY_LIMIT=256m
CONTAINER_CPU_LIMIT=0.5
CONTAINER_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS=600
CONTAINER_NETWORK=agent-sandbox     # Docker network name
```

## Design Section 4: Networking & Security

**Docker Network:**
- Create a dedicated bridge network: `agent-sandbox`
- Sidecar containers are attached to this network
- The host backend (running on host network) is accessible via `host.docker.internal` (Docker Desktop) or `--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway` (Linux)

**Allowed network traffic from sidecar:**
- Outbound to `host.docker.internal:10000` (credential proxy + MCP server) — **only**
- All other egress is blocked via iptables rules on the Docker network, or via gVisor's network filtering
- No inter-container communication (containers cannot reach each other)

**Security hardening per container:**
- `--runtime=runsc` — gVisor intercepts all syscalls
- `--read-only` — root filesystem is read-only (use tmpfs for `/tmp`)
- `--tmpfs /tmp:size=50m` — limited writable temp space
- `--cap-drop=ALL` — drop all Linux capabilities
- `--security-opt=no-new-privileges` — prevent privilege escalation
- `--user node` — run as non-root
- `--memory` / `--cpus` — resource limits
- No volume mounts to host filesystem
- No access to Docker socket
- Auto-removal: `--rm` flag + forced cleanup after max lifetime

**Credential flow (unchanged):**
1. Backend creates short-lived UUID token via `proxy_token_store`
2. UUID passed to sidecar as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env var
3. Sidecar's Claude CLI sends requests to `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (host proxy)
4. Proxy validates UUID → swaps for real key → forwards to Anthropic
5. Token revoked when session ends

**MCP tool access:**
- The MCP server (`execute_sql` tool) runs on the host
- Sidecar reaches it via the host network (`host.docker.internal:10000`)
- MCP requests are scoped to the session's DuckDB instance via session ID

## Design Section 5: Error Handling & Graceful Degradation

**Container startup failures:**
- If Docker daemon is unavailable or gVisor runtime isn't installed, fall back to the current subprocess model (when `CONTAINER_ENABLED=true` but runtime is missing)
- Log a warning on fallback so operators know to install gVisor
- Health check with retries (3 attempts, 1s interval) before routing first query

**Mid-session failures:**
- If the container crashes during a query, return an error SSE event to the frontend
- Do not auto-restart — the session is invalidated (user starts a new conversation)
- Credential proxy token is revoked in the `finally` block regardless

**Resource exhaustion:**
- OOM kill: container is auto-removed, error event sent to frontend
- CPU throttling: handled by Docker's `--cpus` (no kill, just slower)
- Max lifetime exceeded: `cleanup_expired()` forcefully removes the container, sends timeout error

**Graceful shutdown:**
- On backend shutdown, iterate all active containers and remove them
- Register a shutdown hook in FastAPI's `lifespan` to clean up

**Feature flag:**
- `CONTAINER_ENABLED=true/false` — when false, the existing subprocess model is used unchanged
- This allows gradual rollout and easy rollback

content.text:
Great question — this is an important deployment consideration. Let me be direct:

**This architecture will NOT work on Render or most PaaS platforms** (Heroku, Railway, etc.) because:
- PaaS platforms run your app inside a container already
- You can't run Docker (or gVisor) inside their containers without privileged mode, which they don't grant
- gVisor requires specific kernel support

**Where it works:**
| Environment | Support | Notes |
|-------------|---------|-------|
| Self-hosted / bare metal | Full | Install Docker + gVisor directly |
| Cloud VMs (EC2, GCP, Azure) | Full | Install Docker + gVisor on the VM |
| Kubernetes | Full | gVisor as `RuntimeClass`, sidecar as a pod |
| Render / Railway / Heroku | No | Use existing subprocess model (feature flag off) |
| Fly.io | Partial | Firecracker VMs, Docker possible but gVisor unlikely |

**The design accounts for this via the feature flag:**
- `CONTAINER_ENABLED=false` (default on Render) → uses existing subprocess model unchanged
- `CONTAINER_ENABLED=true` (self-hosted/k8s) → uses containerized sidecar with gVisor
- Both paths produce identical SSE output to the frontend — **no frontend changes needed either way**

This means the existing Render deployment continues to work exactly as it does today, while self-hosted or Kubernetes deployments get the enhanced security boundary.

# Credential Proxy Design

**Date:** 2026-02-21
**Status:** Approved

## Problem

The server runs `claude-agent-sdk` which spawns Claude Code CLI as a subprocess. The subprocess inherits the parent process environment, including `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. A malicious user could craft a prompt to extract this token (e.g., `import os; print(os.environ)`), compromising the shared server account.

## Solution

A local reverse proxy runs inside the FastAPI app. Each chat session receives a short-lived UUID token. The Claude Code subprocess is given this UUID plus a `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointing to the local proxy. The proxy validates the UUID and swaps it for the real `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` before forwarding to `api.anthropic.com`.

Even if a user extracts the UUID via prompt injection, it is useless outside `localhost` and expires when the chat session ends.

## Architecture

```
[Server startup]
  1. Read real token from CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN env var → store in memory

[POST /api/chat]
  2. Generate session UUID token
  3. Register UUID → {expiry} in ActiveSessionTokens (TTL = chat session)
  4. Pass to ClaudeAgentOptions(
       env={
         "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN": "<session-uuid>",
         "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:10000/anthropic",
       }
     )
  5. Claude Code subprocess sends Bearer <session-uuid> to local proxy

[/anthropic/{path:path}]
  6. Extract Bearer token from Authorization header
  7. Validate it's a registered, non-expired session UUID
  8. Replace Authorization → "Bearer <real CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN>"
  9. Forward full request + body to https://api.anthropic.com/{path}
 10. Stream response back to Claude Code subprocess

[SSE done/error event in agent.py]
 11. Revoke session UUID from ActiveSessionTokens
```

## Components

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `backend/app/proxy.py` | New — `ProxyTokenStore` + `/anthropic/{path}` FastAPI router |
| `backend/app/agent.py` | Inject `env=` in `ClaudeAgentOptions`; accept token arg; revoke on done/error |
| `backend/app/main.py` | Include proxy router |
| `backend/app/config.py` | Read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from env |

## Key Details

### Env injection

`subprocess_cli.py` builds the subprocess env as:
```python
process_env = {**os.environ, **options.env, ...}
```
`options.env` overrides win, so setting `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in `options.env` prevents the subprocess from seeing the real token in `os.environ`.

### Token store

In-memory dict: `{uuid: expiry_datetime}`. Tokens are created at chat start and deleted on `done`/`error` SSE events. No persistence needed — tokens are ephemeral.

### Proxy forwarding

Uses `httpx.AsyncClient` to forward the full request (method, headers, body) to `https://api.anthropic.com`, streaming the response back. The only header modification is replacing `Authorization`.

### Security properties

- Subprocess never sees real `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`
- UUID token is useless outside `localhost`
- Token expires at session end (revoked explicitly, not just by TTL)
- No OAuth refresh logic needed — proxy forwards the long-lived token as-is

## Out of Scope

- Per-user OAuth (all users share one server account)
- Rate limiting per session (separate concern)
- Persistent token storage
